findings.title: Consume recovery codes and test their one-time-use behavior
findings.body: The new recovery-code validator accepts any code in the original list without removing or marking it used. getCredentials() also rebuilds the credential from that unchanged list, so every login continues to request code 0, previously used codes remain valid, and exhaustion never triggers regeneration. The added integration test performs only one login and therefore passes with this broken recovery-code lifecycle. Make the test provider track consumption and extend the test to verify replay rejection, advancement to the next code, and regeneration after exhaustion.

findings.title: Keep the backwards-compatibility provider compatible with its baseline
findings.body: This provider is explicitly intended to remain source-compatible with Keycloak 4.8.3, but it now imports and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel, which did not exist in that version, and overrides the newer getCredentials SPI method. It can no longer be compiled against the baseline whose compatibility this test is meant to exercise. Put the recovery-code implementation in a separate contemporary test provider rather than changing the legacy compatibility fixture.
